_meta.note: Industry, competition, peers, street, ownership, governance, moat, critiques, gaps and conflicts. Sources dated on or before 30-Sep-2026 only.

industry.outlook: CRISIL (quoted in AR FY26): e-2W sales of 0.60-0.62 crore units by FY30 and 22-25% penetration. Nomura (10-Sep-2026): 22% e-2W penetration by FY30 (45% in scooters).
industry.policy: PM E-DRIVE (Oct-2024, outlay Rs10,900 cr): e-2W demand subsidy Rs2,500/kWh capped at Rs5,000 a vehicle since Apr-2025; extended in Mar-2026 to 31-Jul-2026, then on 11-Aug-2026 to 31-Mar-2028 with e-2W allocation raised by ~Rs1,000 cr to Rs2,767 cr. Delhi's draft EV policy (2026) pushes harder; Haryana following (management, Q1 call). PLI-Auto supports local value addition. Subsidy was 16% of Ather's revenue in FY24, 6% in FY25, 3% in FY26 (AR FY26).
industry.fuel: From early 2026 the West Asia conflict raised petrol prices and caused availability worries; management cites this, plus rising petrol prices, as the main reason e-2W demand jumped (EV searches +75%, Ather searches +118% in Q1FY27).
industry.commodities: Two-wheeler commodity index (HSBC / company) +46% over five quarters to Q1FY27: aluminium, copper, plastics (crude), lithium hydroxide +131%; rare-earth magnet export controls by China (2025).

competition._note: Vahan registrations. FY26 from Autocar Pro / Business Today (1-Apr-2026); Apr-Aug FY27 from Autocar Pro (1-Sep-2026). Ather's own count (wholesale) differs: 262,942 dispatched in FY26.

excluded.BAJAJ-AUTO: Earnings distorted: the Mar-2026 quarter carries ~Rs1,894 cr of other income when Bajaj took control of KTM, and KTM is consolidated from that quarter, so its trailing P/E on 30-Sep-2026 sits on an inflated TTM EPS (same treatment as our Eicher and Hyundai reports).
excluded.ESCORTS: Earnings distorted: FY26 profit inflated by the railway-business sale (PLAYBOOK §7c).

notInSet.OLAELEC: Ola Electric: the only other listed pure EV two-wheeler maker, but loss-making (FY26 EBITDA margin -43%), shrinking and listed only in Aug-2024: no P/E history, so it cannot measure a sector move. Shown in the peer table only.

governance.auditor: Statutory auditor's report on FY26 standalone statements unmodified (AR FY26).
governance.board: Eight directors, three independent (AR FY26): Neelam Dhawan (independent chairperson), Kaushik Dutta and Sanjay Nayak (independent); Tarun Mehta (ED & CEO) and Swapnil Jain (ED & CTO); non-executive directors Pankaj Sood, Vivek Anand and Ram Kuppuswamy (COO-manufacturing at Hero MotoCorp, up for re-appointment at the 2026 AGM). governance.relatedParty: Hero MotoCorp is both the largest shareholder (promoter, 30.0% at Jun-2026) and a direct competitor (Vida e-scooters, 1.44 lakh registrations in FY26). Warrants issued to Hero and the founders at Rs1,260 (25% paid) give them an 18-month option on 79 lakh shares.
governance.esop: Share-based pay Rs58 cr in FY26 (Rs83 cr FY25), ~1.6% of revenue; ESOP 2025 plan approved; grants continue.
governance.fame: FAME-II / PMP show-cause notice (Mar-2023): Ather refunded Rs148 cr of off-board charger prices to customers; Rs9.8 cr outstanding at Mar-2026.

moat: Brand and product
Moderate
Premium e-scooter brand: ASP ~Rs1.61 lakh (Jun-2026), above TVS, Bajaj and Ola; #1 searched EV brand; Rizta took Ather beyond the south
Pricing power is real today (price rises absorbed in Q1FY27), but demand exceeds supply industry-wide, which flatters everyone's pricing
Software and ecosystem
Moderate
AtherStack Pro attach 94%; 6,000+ fast chargers on Ather's LECCS standard (now an Indian standard, 20+ members); non-vehicle revenue 14%
The best evidence of a moat: a recurring, high-margin layer rivals have not matched. But LECCS is now open, and software can be copied
Scale and cost
Weak
2.6 lakh units in FY26 vs TVS 3.4 lakh EVs and 40+ lakh ICE 2Ws; still loss-making on Screener's EBITDA; Hosur capped at 35k/month
No scale advantage against TVS, Bajaj or Hero, which can cross-subsidise EVs from profitable ICE businesses
Distribution
Weak
700 experience centres (Mar-2026) vs thousands of ICE dealers for incumbents
Expanding fast, but incumbents' service reach is far larger
Technology and IP
Moderate
283 patents filed in FY26; in-house battery packs, motor controllers, software, EL platform built for cost
Real engineering depth for a start-up; incumbents' R&D budgets are larger
critiques: Ather is losing share while the market booms: 18.6% in Q4FY26, 16.8% in Q1FY27 and 15.9% in Aug-2026 (Vahan) as TVS and Bajaj grew faster; capacity, not demand, is the limit until AURIC ramps
Incumbents can price e-scooters off ICE profits; Hero, a 30% shareholder, also sells Vida
Gross margin is exposed to lithium, copper and rare earths; Q1FY27 showed a 5.6pp commodity hit

The stock already prices a lot: the street pays 5.5-7x forward EV/Sales for a company that has not yet made an annual operating profit; profitable 2W makers trade on far lower sales multiples (peer table)
Konarc lowers ASP and may cannibalise Rizta
Subsidy is small now (3% of revenue) but policy still matters: state EV policies and the PM E-DRIVE cap
gaps: QIP issue expenses (not disclosed by 30-Sep-2026): we use gross proceeds of Rs1,300 cr.
Consolidated balance sheet at Jun-2026 (Ather does not publish quarterly balance sheets); cash at 30-Sep-2026 is therefore Mar-2026 plus the equity raised, not a reported figure.
Q3FY26 quarterly P&L lines other than revenue and loss: derived as FY26 less the other three quarters (Screener omits the quarter).
Reason why 15-20% of Q1FY27 vehicles were sold without PM E-DRIVE subsidy (management did not explain).
FY27 capex guidance: management gave none; we anchor to the unused IPO allocation for AURIC (Rs788 cr) and R&D (Rs478 cr).
Konarc price list for Z variants and its revenue per unit: not disclosed by 30-Sep.
Valuation methods and estimates of Axis, CLSA, JPMorgan, Nirmal Bang, HSBC and Ambit: only targets are reported in our sources (n.d.).
